newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire's religious leaders call for ceasefire.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's religious leaders call for ceasefire.

text.p: Leaders of Zaire's main religious denominations called on Saturday for the two chief protagonists in the country's seven-month-old civil war to meet to work out conditions for a ceasefire.

At a news conference in the Zairean capital, the leaders of the Catholic, Protestant, Moslem, Kimbanguist and Orthodox faiths said they would be sending envoys to meet rebel leader Laurent Kabila in a bid to persuade him to enter negotiations.
They said they had held numerous meetings this month with diplomatic representatives, politicians, civilian leaders and had been received last week by President Mobutu Sese Seko.

"As spiritual fathers of President Mobutu and of Mr. Laurent Desire Kabila, we emplore them in the interest of the entire Zairean nation, to meet and seek a peaceful solution and the reconciliation of all children of Zaire," the religious leaders said in a statement.
"We emplore Zairean politicians to finish their sterile and egotistical disputes which have plunged the people into suffering," the statement added.
Monseigneur Bokeleale Itofob, a leader of the Protestant faith, said the group would be contacting Kabila early next week in order to seek a meeting with him.

He said that for years church leaders had been emploring the political class to find lasting solutions to Zaire's problems in order to avert catastrophe. "They didn't listen to their fathers," he said.
International diplomatic efforts to bring Mobutu and Kabila together are floundering as the two protagonists have failed to agree on a venue for talks.
Kabila says his troops will use overwhelming force to march on the sprawling Zairean capital of five million people soon to end Mobutu's 32-year rule.
